text: A smoke test is a quick, basic check that a deployed system actually works end-to-end, run immediately after deployment and before it carries any real traffic or real data. It's not a full test suite, and it's not meant to catch every bug — it's meant to catch the handful of showstopper problems before anyone finds out the hard way, which is exactly the step this chapter has been building toward since Lesson 9.

The concrete test here is simple: write a test file to storage from the VM, using the identity wired up in Lesson 11, then read it back. On Azure, that's a blob upload and download authenticated with --auth-mode login; on AWS, an aws s3 cp up and back down. If the upload succeeds, Lesson 9's network path and Lesson 11's identity grant both work. If it fails, you know exactly where to look, because that's all this test touches.

Reaching storage confirms the network and identity chain, but not that the application itself is running correctly. A basic curl against a health endpoint closes that gap — a 200 OK means the application process is up and responding, not just that the VM is reachable. An environment that passes the storage round trip but fails this check still isn't done.

Skipping this step doesn't eliminate the risk — it delays discovery to a worse moment: a misconfigured role assignment found when a real user hits an error in production, or inherited by a teammate weeks later with no idea whether it's new or was always broken. Running it now, while you still remember exactly what you built, is the cheapest this problem will ever be to diagnose.

That's Chapter 3 done — network, compute, storage, and the identity connecting them, proven to actually work, not just assumed to. Chapter 4 picks up right here: standing up the monitoring that would tell you if any of this broke, before you find out from a user instead.
